Sabra and Shatila

Massacre · 1982-09-16 · During Israeli occupation of West Beirut, Lebanon War

16-18 Sept 1982
Date

Israeli Accountability
Location, thenSabra and Shatila refugee camps, Beirut, Lebanon (under Israeli military control)
Location, nowSabra and Shatila, Beirut, Lebanon; Camps still exist; memorial sites established
PerpetratorsLebanese Forces (Phalangist militia); Israeli Defense Forces (facilitation and responsibility); Defense Minister Ariel Sharon (personal responsibility per Kahan Commission)
ClassificationWar Crime; Crimes Against Humanity; Genocide (UNSC Res 521; Kahan Commission)

Summary

The Sabra and Shatila massacre occurred during Israel's 1982 invasion of Lebanon ('Operation Peace for Galilee'). After the assassination of Lebanese President-elect Bachir Gemayel on September 14, 1982, Israeli Defense Minister Ariel Sharon ordered IDF forces to occupy West Beirut, ostensibly to maintain order. On September 16, Sharon authorized Lebanese Phalangist militias to enter the Sabra and Shatila Palestinian refugee camps, claiming they would 'mop up' remaining PLO fighters—though PLO forces had evacuated weeks earlier under international agreement.

For approximately 40 hours (September 16-18), Phalangist militiamen systematically killed Palestinian civilians, including women, children, and elderly persons. Israeli forces surrounded the camps, controlled all entry and exit points, provided logistical support, and fired illumination flares throughout the nights allowing the killings to continue after dark. Israeli commanders received reports of civilian massacres but did not intervene. Methods included shooting, stabbing, decapitation, mutilation. Bodies were dumped in mass graves or left in streets.

The exact death toll remains disputed. Lebanon's official investigation documented approximately 800 killed; the Palestinian Red Crescent estimated 3,500; various international sources cite 2,000-3,500. The Israeli Kahan Commission investigated and found Defense Minister Sharon bore 'personal responsibility' for the massacre, recommending his removal. Sharon resigned as Defense Minister but remained in cabinet without portfolio, later serving as Israeli Prime Minister (2001-2006). Multiple international legal attempts to prosecute him failed.

Timeline

1982-09-14 00:00:00 Bachir Gemayel assassinatedLebanese President-elect Bachir Gemayel (Phalangist leader, Israeli ally) killed by bomb in East Beirut. Israeli military leadership decides to occupy West Beirut and send Phalangists into camps. — Kahan Commission Report - Background
15 September, evening IDF occupies West BeirutIsraeli forces enter West Beirut in violation of ceasefire agreement. Surround Sabra and Shatila camps. Meeting at Defense Ministry: Sharon, Chief of Staff Eitan, and Phalangist commanders plan camp entry. — Kahan Commission - Decision Making
2026-09-16 17:00:00 Phalangists enter campsApproximately 150 Phalangist militiamen enter Shatila camp through IDF lines. Israeli officers coordinate entry. IDF controls all access points, provides maps, logistics. Killing begins immediately. — Kahan Commission - Operational Timeline
16 September, night First night of killingsSystematic house-to-house killings. IDF fires illumination flares throughout night allowing massacre to continue after dark. Israeli officers at forward command posts receive reports of civilian killings but do not intervene. — Robert Fisk - The Independent, September 18-19, 1982
2026-09-17 00:00:00 Massacre continuesKillings intensify. Reports reach IDF commanders of women and children being killed. Chief of Staff Eitan informed but orders Phalangists to continue. More militiamen enter camps. Bulldozers brought in to bury bodies. — Kahan Commission - Day Two Events
17 September, night Second nightIDF continues providing illumination flares. Mass killings continue. Bodies accumulate in streets and mass graves. Some victims tortured before death; evidence of sexual violence. — ICRC Documentation 1982
18 September, morning International alarmReports of massacre reach international media. US pressures Israel to halt operation. Israeli cabinet meets; orders Phalangists to leave camps. — US State Department Records 1982
2026-09-18 08:00:00 Phalangists withdrawMilitiamen leave camps after approximately 40 hours. Bodies litter streets. Mass graves discovered. International journalists, including Robert Fisk, enter camps and document carnage. — Robert Fisk - 'Pity the Nation' (1990)
1982-09-25 00:00:00 Mass protests in Israel400,000 Israelis (10% of population) protest in Tel Aviv demanding investigation. Largest protest in Israeli history. Pressure forces government to establish commission. — Peace Now Historical Documentation
1982-09-28 00:00:00 Kahan Commission establishedIsraeli government establishes Commission of Inquiry headed by Supreme Court President Yitzhak Kahan to investigate Israeli responsibility. — Kahan Commission - Establishment Order
1983-02-08 00:00:00 Kahan Commission report releasedCommission finds Defense Minister Sharon bore 'personal responsibility' for not preventing massacre. Recommends his removal. Chief of Staff Eitan and others also found negligent. Sharon resigns as Defense Minister but remains in cabinet. — Kahan Commission - Full Report
1982-12-16 00:00:00 UN condemns massacreUN General Assembly Resolution 37/123 D declares massacre 'act of genocide.' Overwhelmingly passed. Israel rejects findings. — UN General Assembly Resolution 37/123

Testimony

Robert FiskEntered camps morning of September 18. 'There were women lying in the doorways, shot in the back and the front...I came across a group of women and children clustered around a dead man lying in a pile of garbage. On my right was a young Palestinian woman...holding a tiny baby to her body. The baby had been shot through the back of the head.' Described systematic nature of killings. — Pity the Nation: Lebanon at War' (1990); The Independent September 18-19, 1982
Kahan CommissionOfficial findings: Sharon bore 'personal responsibility' for not preventing massacre. 'It is impossible to justify the Minister of Defense's disregard of the danger of acts of revenge...and his lack of involvement in the course of events.' Recommended Sharon's removal; found Chief of Staff Eitan and others negligent. — Commission of Inquiry into Events at Refugee Camps in Beirut - Final Report, February 8, 1983
Ellen SiegelPresent during massacre. Witnessed killings, attempted to help wounded. Testified: 'I saw Israeli soldiers standing on rooftops watching as the Phalangists went from house to house.' Described seeing bodies of women and children, mass graves being dug. — Testimony to human rights organizations; documented in UN reports
Ariel SharonInitially denied Israeli responsibility. After Kahan Commission: accepted 'indirect' responsibility but claimed could not have foreseen massacre. In autobiography 'Warrior' (1989): defended decision to send Phalangists into camps. Never expressed remorse. Resigned as Defense Minister but remained in cabinet. — Warrior: An Autobiography' (1989); Official statements to Kahan Commission
Palestinian SurvivorsSurvivors described militiamen going house to house, executing families, separating men from women and children before killing. One survivor: 'They killed my husband, my three sons, my daughter. They killed them in front of me.' Another: 'They made us stand against the wall. They shot everyone. I only survived because bodies fell on top of me.' — Collected by Lebanese government commission, human rights organizations, Palestinian Red Crescent
Israeli Soldiers (anonymous testimonies)Several soldiers later testified they reported civilian killings to commanders but were ordered not to intervene. One: 'We saw them killing civilians...we reported it up the chain of command. Nothing was done.' Multiple soldiers confirmed IDF fired illumination flares throughout nights. — Kahan Commission testimony; later interviews with Breaking the Silence

War crimes

Systematic Massacre of CiviliansHouse-to-house killings over 40+ hours. Victims predominantly women, children, elderly. Men of fighting age had mostly evacuated with PLO forces. Methods: shooting, stabbing, axe attacks, decapitation. Kahan Commission confirmed systematic nature of killings. — Kahan Commission Report
Torture and MutilationJournalists documented bodies with signs of torture: mutilations, dismemberment, disfigurement. Pregnant women killed; bodies desecrated. Robert Fisk: 'I saw dead babies, blackened in the heat, already decomposing. I saw dead women lying in the road.' — UN Documentation
Sexual ViolenceEvidence of rape and sexual violence. Bodies of women found partially clothed or unclothed. Lebanese investigating commission documented sexual assaults. — ICRC Reports
Mass Graves and Body DisposalBulldozers brought in during massacre to bury bodies in mass graves. Some victims buried alive. Systematic effort to conceal scale of killings. Many bodies never recovered or identified.
Israeli FacilitationIDF surrounded camps, controlled all entry/exit, provided maps, coordinated Phalangist entry, fired illumination flares at night enabling killing to continue, received reports of massacre but did not intervene for 40 hours. — Kahan Commission - Israeli Responsibility
Killing of Children and InfantsMultiple documented cases of infants and young children killed. Entire families executed together. Orphans found alive among corpses. Robert Fisk described finding children's bodies in rubble. — Journalist Accounts

Legal classification

Fourth Geneva Convention (1949) ViolationsArticle 27: Protected persons entitled to respect for persons, honor, family rights, religious convictions. Shall be protected against violence, intimidation, insults, public curiosity. Systematically violated.
Command Responsibility DoctrineSuperior responsibility: Israeli commanders knew or should have known massacre was occurring and failed to prevent or punish. Kahan Commission explicitly found this.
UN General Assembly FindingsResolution 37/123 D (1982): Declared massacre 'an act of genocide.' Passed 123-0 with 22 abstentions. Israel rejected characterization but did not contest factual findings.
Attempts at Individual Criminal AccountabilityBelgium (2001): Survivors filed case under universal jurisdiction law. Belgian Supreme Court initially allowed prosecution of Sharon. Law later amended under US/Israeli pressure; case dismissed.
Fourth Geneva Convention (1949) ViolationsArticle 32: Prohibited physical suffering or extermination of protected persons. Massacre constituted extermination.
Command Responsibility DoctrineDuty to prevent: Under customary international law, commanders must take feasible measures to prevent crimes by forces under their control. Sharon and IDF command failed this duty.
UN General Assembly FindingsGenocide Convention analysis: Acts committed with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, Palestinian group as such. Deliberate killing of members of group (Article II(a)).
Attempts at Individual Criminal AccountabilityUniversal jurisdiction principle: War crimes and crimes against humanity prosecutable anywhere. However, political considerations prevented prosecution.
Fourth Geneva Convention (1949) ViolationsArticle 147 (Grave Breaches): Willful killing, torture, inhuman treatment of protected persons constitute war crimes. All present in Sabra and Shatila.
Command Responsibility DoctrinePersonal responsibility: Kahan Commission: Sharon bore 'personal responsibility' for not ordering prevention of harm to civilians despite foreseeable risks.
Attempts at Individual Criminal AccountabilityICC jurisdiction: Rome Statute not in effect in 1982; retroactive prosecution impossible. However, acts would constitute crimes against humanity and war crimes under current law.
Fourth Geneva Convention (1949) ViolationsOccupying Power Responsibility: Israel as occupying power in West Beirut bore legal responsibility to protect civilian population under its control.

Commanders

1928-2014 Ariel SharonKahan Commission found Sharon bore 'personal responsibility' for massacre. Authorized Phalangist entry into camps despite foreseeable risk to civilians. Failed to prevent killings despite receiving reports. Recommended for removal as Defense Minister. Resigned but remained in cabinet. Later served as Prime Minister (2001-2006). Multiple international prosecution attempts failed.
1929-2004 Rafael EitanOverall command of IDF operations in Lebanon. Coordinated Phalangist entry into camps. Received reports of civilian massacres but ordered militias to continue. Kahan Commission found him negligent. Recommended for removal but already scheduled to retire. Later entered politics; never prosecuted.
1913-1992 Menachem BeginPrime Minister during Lebanon War (Operation Peace for Galilee). Authorized invasion and occupation of West Beirut. Kahan Commission found he should have been more involved in preventing foreseeable harm. Not recommended for removal. Resigned 1983, partly due to Lebanon War failures.
1915-2012 Yitzhak ShamirForeign Minister during massacre. Kahan Commission noted he knew of Phalangist entry but did not object. Later became Prime Minister (1983-84, 1986-92). Never held accountable for role in events.
1956-2002 Elie HobeikaLebanese Forces commander who led Phalangist militiamen into camps. Directly responsible for organizing and executing massacre. Never prosecuted. Assassinated in 2002 car bombing in Beirut before planned testimony in Belgian universal jurisdiction case.
Unknown Fadi FremSenior Lebanese Forces commander who led militiamen during massacre. Directed ground operations inside camps. Never prosecuted. Identity and fate poorly documented.
